name: EBESU Robata & Sushi
desc: Tiny modern Japanese bistro in the Downtown Plano Arts District that grills over binchotan charcoal and got James Beard attention in 2022. Get the robata skewers and whatever nigiri is on the seasonal special board. Reserve ahead, it seats maybe 30 people and weekends vanish fast.

reviews.text: Best sushi in Collin County and it is not close.
Tiny room so book early, but the skewers are worth it.

name: Rokhat Grill
desc: Family run Uzbek halal kitchen off Central Expressway doing plov, samsa, manti and kebabs from scratch every morning. Order the marvarid kebab plate and a lepyoshka bread to tear apart. Open until 11pm so it is a real late night option in Plano.

reviews.text: Plov tastes like my grandmother made it. Portions are huge.
Samsa straight out of the oven, flaky and unreal.

name: Millstone Bakery
desc: Belgian family bakery on Legacy running since 2014, now run by the founder's daughter. Brioche cinnamon rolls, real Belgian chocolate eclairs and macarons, plus actual Liege waffles on the last weekend of every month. Show up before noon or the good stuff is gone.

reviews.text: Croissants better than anything I had in Paris, genuinely.
Waffle weekend is the move. Get there early.

name: Hong Yuan Dumplings & Noodles
desc: Strip mall spot on West Park that D Magazine flagged for having some of the best soup dumplings and hand pulled noodles in North Texas. Pork xiao long bao and the Lanzhou beef noodle soup are the order, chili volcano noodles if you want heat. Quick lunch energy, go off peak so your food comes out together.

reviews.text: XLB wrappers are thin and the broth actually gushes.
Food is elite, service gets slammed on weekends.

name: ChongQing House
desc: Small unfussy Sichuan room on the Central Expressway service road that regulars swear is the most authentic Chinese in Plano. Fish fillet soup with pickled vegetables is the sleeper hit, then anything numbing off the Chongqing side of the menu. Cheap, fast, family style portions, closed Tuesdays.

reviews.text: Pickled veg fish soup is a whole personality change.
Nothing fancy inside. The food does all the work.

name: Crepes 4 U
desc: A crepe counter hidden inside the side entrance of Jusgo Supermarket on Legacy, run since 2007 by Paul, who trained in Paris and will talk to you the whole time. Brownie plus hazelnut plus ice cream runs under six bucks. Grocery store lighting, unbelievable dessert, perfect random weeknight stop.

reviews.text: Mr Paul remembers your order. Nicest man in Plano.
Inside a grocery store and still the best dessert here.

name: Grand Tandoori Restaurant
desc: East Plano Pakistani and North Indian kitchen that locals have slept on for years. Chicken karahi, beef seekh kebab and the Hyderabadi style biryani are the reasons to drive over, and the lunch buffet is stacked. Bright, clean, family run, zabiha halal.

reviews.text: Karahi tastes like a home kitchen, not a restaurant.
Buffet is a steal and the tandoori meats stay juicy.

name: Taipei Station Cafe
desc: Family owned Taiwanese hole in the wall tucked in a Parker Road strip center. The beef noodle soup broth simmers for days and the popcorn chicken and pork chop rice plates are just as good. Hours are short and change often, so check before you drive out.

reviews.text: Closest thing to a Taipei night market bowl out here.
Tiny place, food comes out fast.

name: Express Kabob
desc: Family owned Afghan and Persian halal spot that a lot of DFW people will argue is the best Afghan food in the metroplex. Kabuli pulao with the lamb shank is the signature, lamb kabob if you want something quicker. Counter service, food hits your table in under ten minutes.

reviews.text: Kabuli pulao here beats places I ate in Kabul.
Fast, cheap, huge portions. Lamb shank falls apart.

name: Cho Dang Village
desc: Korean tofu house on Legacy where the soondubu comes out volcano hot and loaded with seafood or beef. Banchan spread is generous and people genuinely argue their kimchi is the best in DFW. Gets packed at lunch but the turnover is quick.

reviews.text: Soondubu still bubbling when it hits the table. Perfect.
Kimchi alone is worth the drive. Always busy.

name: Hoshi Japanese Cafe
desc: Tiny Japanese street food and sweets cafe on Coit doing obanyaki and pandayaki, those custard filled griddle cakes that look absurdly cute on camera. Grab a matcha and a couple of fillings to compare. Closed Tuesdays, and the after school crowd fills it up around 4pm.

reviews.text: Custard obanyaki hot off the griddle, so good.
Cutest little cafe in Plano and the matcha is legit.

name: Yatai Ramen Izakaya
desc: Coit Road izakaya where the tonkotsu broth is thick enough to coat the spoon and the small plates are the real move. Order karaage and takoyaki alongside the ramen and split everything. Dim, loud, good late dinner spot with friends.

reviews.text: Tonkotsu is rich without being greasy. Rare here.
Get the karaage. Ramen alone undersells this place.

name: Boba Republic
desc: Local boba shop in the Legacy Drive Asian plaza that quietly outranks every chain in town. Brown sugar milk tea and the fruit teas with real fruit are what people come back for, and you can dial the sweetness properly. Good late study hang, and the parking lot is a whole Asian food crawl on its own.

reviews.text: Pearls are always fresh and chewy. Never a bad cup.
Better than any chain nearby and cheaper too.
